page: Vultr voc-s-2c-16gb-480s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It is configured with 2 shared vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. The system includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 480 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show a split performance profile. The server achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, ranking in the top 10%, and strong single-threaded compression and decompression capabilities. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the average tier, and overall PassMark CPU scores, including encryption and physics tests, are positioned in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed, with average large-block read and write bandwidth but weak cached small-block read bandwidth.

Due to its shared CPU allocation, this server exhibits performance limitations under sustained multi-threaded workloads. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are relatively weak, with web serving falling into the bottom 10%. Large language model inference is also constrained, with 7B model generation rated as poor. Consequently, this server is best suited for memory-intensive but compute-light workloads, such as caching layers, lightweight memory-optimized applications, or development environments that benefit from the 16 GB RAM and fast local NVMe storage but do not require sustained, high-throughput multi-core processing.
description: Vultr voc-s-2c-16gb-480s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 2 shared vCPUs, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a 480 GB NVMe SSD. While single-core CPU performance is highly competitive, ranking in the top 10% in stress-ng benchmarks, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are average. The server exhibits weak performance in database operations, Redis SET transactions, and static web serving, which falls into the bottom 10%. With a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy, non-compute-intensive tasks. It is best suited for lightweight memory-optimized applications, caching, and development environments that require substantial RAM and local NVMe storage but can tolerate shared CPU resource limits.
